tour.name: Nikko Private Day Trip from Tokyo: Toshogu Shrine, Shinkyo Bridge & Kegon Falls
tour.subtitle: A private day in the mountains north of Tokyo with a licensed guide and car: the sacred red Shinkyo bridge, the lavish Toshogu shrine of the first Tokugawa shogun with its three wise monkeys and sleeping cat, lunch of yuba, the Irohazaka hairpin road, Lake Chuzenji and the Kegon waterfall.

tour.overview:
In the mountains 140 kilometres north of Tokyo, among cedar forests planted four centuries ago, lies one of Japan's most extravagant monuments: Toshogu, the shrine where Tokugawa Ieyasu, the shogun who unified Japan in 1603, is enshrined as a god. His grandson Iemitsu rebuilt it in the 1630s with more than 5,000 carvings, painted and gilded, as a statement of the dynasty's power. With the temple of Rinno-ji and the shrine of Futarasan, the shrines and temples of Nikko have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999.

This private day takes you there with a licensed guide and a car. You cross the sacred bridge, explore Toshogu and its famous carvings, walk through the cedar forest to the other shrines, have a lunch of yuba, then climb the Irohazaka road into the mountains to Lake Chuzenji and the Kegon Falls.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 11 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Tokyo
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; about 5 km with many stone steps at the shrines

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Shinkyo bridge.
• Rinno-ji temple.
• Toshogu shrine, the Yomeimon gate, the three monkeys, the sleeping cat and Ieyasu's tomb.
• Futarasan shrine.
• The Irohazaka road.
• Lake Chuzenji and the Kegon Falls.

WHY THIS WORKS
Nikko is a long journey by public transport and the sights are spread over the mountain; with a car you see both the shrines and the lake in one day.

WHO IT SUITS
Anyone interested in Japanese history and art, nature lovers and photographers, especially in autumn.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer a shorter day near Tokyo, choose Kamakura.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The drive takes about 2 hours 30 minutes each way. Mid-October to early November is the peak of autumn colours, with heavy traffic on the Irohazaka; we start early. Nikko is cooler than Tokyo.

days.name: The Shinkyo bridge, Toshogu, Rinno-ji and Futarasan, a yuba lunch, the Irohazaka road, Lake Chuzenji and Kegon Falls
days.description:
What to expect: the mausoleum of the shogun and the mountain lakes and waterfalls of Nikko, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at 7:00 for the drive north, about 2 hours 30 minutes. You arrive at the Shinkyo bridge, a lacquered red bridge over the Daiya river, built where, according to legend, two giant snakes formed a bridge to let the Buddhist monk Shodo cross in the 8th century; for centuries only shoguns and imperial envoys could walk on it.

You climb into the cedar forest to Rinno-ji, the great Buddhist temple founded by Shodo, whose main hall holds three gilded statues of Buddha almost 8 metres tall. A path lined with stone lanterns leads to Toshogu. Your guide shows you the five-storey pagoda, the sacred stable with the carving of the three wise monkeys – see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil – which tells the story of a life in eight panels, and the Yomeimon gate, so richly carved with 500 figures of people, animals and flowers that it was said you could look at it all day. Inside the inner precinct you find the tiny carving of the sleeping cat, Nemuri-neko, and climb 207 stone steps through the forest to Ieyasu's bronze tomb. You end at Futarasan, a shrine to the three sacred mountains of Nikko, with its 'ghost lantern'.

Lunch features yuba, the delicate skin formed on heated soy milk, a speciality of Nikko since monks made it for their vegetarian diet. In the afternoon you drive up the Irohazaka, a road of 48 hairpin bends – one for each letter of the old Japanese alphabet – to Lake Chuzenji, formed by an eruption of Mount Nantai, whose cone rises above it. A lift takes you 100 metres down to a platform facing the Kegon Falls, which drop 97 metres from the lake into a gorge. You drive back to Tokyo, arriving at about 18:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:00 – Pick-up at your hotel in Tokyo.
09:30 – Shinkyo bridge.
09:45 – Rinno-ji.
10:30 – Toshogu and Ieyasu's tomb (about 1 hour 30 minutes).
12:15 – Futarasan shrine.
12:45 – Yuba lunch.
14:00 – Irohazaka road.
14:30 – Kegon Falls and Lake Chuzenji.
15:45 – Drive back to Tokyo.
18:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Shoes are removed in some halls: wear shoes easy to take off.
• In autumn, traffic on the Irohazaka can be very heavy; we may reverse the day.
• A night at a hot-spring ryokan in Nikko or Kinugawa can be added.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Toshogu, Rinno-ji and Futarasan tickets, Kegon Falls lift, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks with lunch, other temples.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How long is the drive?
faq.answer: About 2 hours 30 minutes each way from central Tokyo, more on weekends. Alternatively, take the Tobu Limited Express train to Nikko and we meet you at the station.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: Toshogu (including the sleeping cat and Ieyasu's tomb), Rinno-ji, Futarasan and the Kegon Falls lift.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, a lunch featuring yuba. Vegetarian diets are easy, as yuba cuisine was created by monks.

faq.question: Is there much walking?
faq.answer: About 5 km with many stone steps, including 207 to Ieyasu's tomb, which you can skip.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children enjoy finding the monkeys and the sleeping cat, the bridge of the snakes and the waterfall. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The shrine area has many steps and gravel paths. The bridge, Lake Chuzenji and the Kegon Falls lift are easy.

faq.question: When are the autumn colours?
faq.answer: Usually from early October at the lake to early November at the shrines. It is the most beautiful and busiest time.

faq.question: Can we stay overnight?
faq.answer: Yes. Nikko and Kinugawa have lovely hot-spring ryokans; a second day can include the Senjogahara marsh or Edo Wonderland.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not customary in Japan, and no one will expect it.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes easy to remove, and warm layers: Nikko is cooler than Tokyo, and the lake is at 1,270 metres.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: May to June for fresh greenery, October to early November for autumn colours. Winter can bring snow and closures on the mountain road.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
